body_ar:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين، السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته.

أما بعد فإن الله تعالى استخلف الناس فيما جعل تحت أيديهم من المال، وجعل من المال مالا مشتركا بين المسلمين، ينتفع به فقراؤهم وأغنياؤهم على حد السواء، أو يكون مختصا بشريحة من شرائحهم وفئة من فئاتهم، وهذا هو المال العام الذي هو حق مشترك للمسلمين تشترك فيه الأجيال اللاحقة مع الأجيال الموجودة.
body_en:
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds. I pray for blessing and peace upon the one who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his practice until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

To proceed: God, exalted, has made people stewards in the wealth He has placed under their hands. And He has made some wealth to be held in common among the Muslims, from which their poor and their rich benefit equally, or which is particular to one stratum among their strata and one category among their categories. This is public money, which is a right held in common by the Muslims, in which the generations to come share along with the generations now present.

flags.context: the page as served: the khuṭbat al-ḥājah plus a single sentence of definition, then the download link
options: render faithfully, mark as an excerpt, and do not display as an article
display as a short article on public money
flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY — STYLE GUIDE §9 AND §10. What the page publishes is the opening formula and one sentence defining what public money is. The title announces the inviolability of public money — a subject with obvious contemporary political weight in the Sheikh's own setting — and not one word of the ruling on it appears. Everything is in the .docx download. This must carry an excerpt banner and must not be presented as the Sheikh's position on the misuse of public funds.

flags.arabic: استخلف الناس فيما جعل تحت أيديهم من المال
flags.context: the theological premise on which the lecture is built
options: has made people stewards in the wealth He has placed under their hands
has made people successors in the wealth He has put in their hands
has appointed people as vicegerents over the wealth under their control
flags.note: istakhlafa carries the sense of appointing someone as a khalīfah, a successor or deputy holding something on behalf of another, and it is the root of the argument that follows: wealth is held in trust, not owned outright. 'Stewards' carries that; 'successors' is more literal but reads oddly in English. Since the argument this premise supports is not in the published text, the rendering cannot be checked against its conclusion and is flagged as provisional.

translator_notes: The date carried here is the CMS record date. Across this whole slice the site serves a bulk-upload timestamp of 19-23 December 2010, which is when the written archive was loaded into the site, not when the Sheikh gave the answer. date_is_cms_upload is set true. The real date of composition is not recoverable from the page and has not been guessed.
The opening is the khuṭbat al-ḥājah, the standard formula with which the Sheikh begins a lecture. It is rendered in full rather than abbreviated, since it is part of the published text.

EXCERPT ONLY. The page publishes the opening and breaks off; the full text sits behind the .docx download recorded in source_download_link. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and the thought has not been completed. The site must render this with an excerpt banner, never as a whole article.
This record is a lecture opening, not a fatwa, and is typed transcript for that reason.
The final clause — that later generations share in public money along with the present ones — is the Sheikh's own and is stated without evidence in the published text. It has not been elaborated.
